statements.text: Overexpression of the hub HvBBX genes in barley improves plant survival under salt stress.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: highlights promising candidate genes for improving stress tolerance in barley
statements.note: The hub genes are proposed as candidates; no overexpression or functional test of stress tolerance is reported.

statements.text: Across 20 barley accessions, the pangenome analysis found 360 HvBBX genes falling into 20 orthologous groups.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: A pangenome wide analysis of 20 barley accessions identified 360 HvBBXs, which were clustered into 20 orthologous gene groups
statements.note: The abstract gives exactly these counts: 20 accessions, 360 HvBBXs, 20 orthologous gene groups.

statements.text: Co-expression network analysis under salt stress identified two HvBBX genes as hub genes associated with chloroplast-related processes and salt tolerance.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: weighted gene co expression network analysis under salt stress identified four HvBBXs, HvBBX.CR2, HvBBX.SC3, HvBBX.CR11, and HvBBX.CR14, as hub genes
statements.note: Four hub genes were identified, not two.

statements.text: DNA transposons were preferentially enriched in the regulatory regions flanking HvBBX genes.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Analysis of transposable elements showed preferential enrichment of DNA transposons in regulatory regions flanking HvBBXs
statements.note: The abstract reports preferential enrichment of DNA transposons in HvBBX-flanking regulatory regions.

statements.text: Before chemotherapy began, ctDNA was detected in two thirds of the patients (10 of 15).
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: ctDNA was detectable in 10 of 15 patients prior to ddMVAC
statements.note: Ten of 15 patients had detectable ctDNA before ddMVAC, which is two thirds.

statements.text: Longitudinal variant allele frequency changes diverged from treatment response in most patients.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: Longitudinal changes in variant allele frequency largely mirrored treatment response, although discrepancies were observed in two cases
statements.note: VAF changes largely mirrored response; discrepancies occurred in only two cases.

statements.text: Patients with detectable ctDNA before ddMVAC had shorter overall survival than those without detectable ctDNA.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: ctDNA was detectable in 10 of 15 patients prior to ddMVAC and showed a trend toward association with total tumor volume
statements.note: Pre-treatment ctDNA is related to tumor volume and later to treatment response; survival is not analysed.

statements.text: Patients whose metastases were confined to the lung had limited ctDNA detection.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: In contrast, ctDNA detection was limited in cases with only pulmonary metastases.
statements.note: The abstract states ctDNA detection was limited in cases with only pulmonary metastases.

statements.text: The ratio of solo to intact LTRs was negatively correlated with genome size across Pucciniomycotina.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: we observed a strong positive correlation between solo:intact LTR ratio (strength of LTR-RT removal) and genome size ( r = 0.65)
statements.note: The correlation was strongly positive (r = 0.65), not negative.

statements.text: Solo LTR count tracked genome size almost linearly across the fungal genomes analysed, with a correlation of 0.98.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: a near-linear correlation between solo LTR count and genome size ( r = 0.98)
statements.note: The abstract reports a near-linear correlation of r = 0.98 between solo LTR count and genome size.

statements.text: The myrtle rust pathogen Austropuccinia psidii has a genome size of about 1018 Mb.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: myrtle rust ( Austropuccinia psidii ), which drastically expanded its genome size to 1018 Mb
statements.note: The abstract gives the expanded A. psidii genome size as 1018 Mb.

statements.text: Solo LTR remnants account for the majority of the A. psidii genome sequence.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: a near-linear correlation between solo LTR count and genome size ( r = 0.98)
statements.note: The correlation links solo LTR count to genome size, but the fraction of the genome occupied by solo LTRs is never given.

statements.text: The SOS splicing pathway works independently of the spliceosome and relies on AKAP17A, CAAP1, and RTCB.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: This spliceosome-independent pathway, mediated by AKAP17A, CAAP1, and RTCB
statements.note: The abstract describes SOS splicing as spliceosome-independent and mediated by these three factors.

statements.text: Loss of SOS splicing components is lethal in mammals.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: The lethality of ADAR loss underscores its role as the mechanism mitigating purifying selection on TEs
statements.note: Lethality is reported for ADAR loss only; the consequence of losing AKAP17A, CAAP1 or RTCB is not discussed.

statements.text: SOS splicing removes retrotransposon sequences from mRNAs by recognizing hairpins formed by long terminal repeats.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: excises DNA transposons from mRNAs, thereby restoring gene sequence. This spliceosome-independent pathway, mediated by AKAP17A, CAAP1, and RTCB, recognizes dsRNA hairpins formed by inverted terminal repeats (ITRs)
statements.note: SOS splicing targets DNA transposons via inverted terminal repeat hairpins, not retrotransposons via LTRs.

statements.text: ADAR-mediated editing dampens MDA5-driven innate immune responses to TE-derived double-stranded RNAs.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: ADAR-mediated A-to-I RNA editing suppresses the MDA5-triggered innate immune responses to TE-derived dsRNAs
statements.note: The abstract states that ADAR editing suppresses MDA5-triggered immune responses to TE-derived dsRNAs.

statements.text: TE transcription was higher in the Bt-resistant strain than in the susceptible strain.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: The analysis of differential expression of TEs in susceptible and resistant strains, challenged and not challenged with Bacillus thuringiensis ( Bt ) from in silico analysis
statements.note: Strains were compared, but the abstract reports only that Bt exposure regulates TE transcription, with no direction between resistant and susceptible strains.

statements.text: In silico differential expression analysis indicated that Bt exposure had no effect on TE transcription in the caterpillar.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: indicated that exposure to Bt can regulate the transcription of mobile genetic elements in the velvetbean caterpillar
statements.note: The analysis indicated that Bt exposure does regulate TE transcription.

statements.text: Retrotransposons made up roughly 71% of the TE-like transcripts identified, outnumbering DNA transposons by more than two to one.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Retrotransposons accounted for 71.2% (595 sequences) of the identified elements, while DNA transposons were less abundant, with 240 annotations (28.8%).
statements.note: 595 retrotransposon versus 240 DNA transposon annotations is 71.2% versus 28.8%, a ratio above 2:1.

statements.text: SINE3/5S and Gypsy were the most abundant of the 30 TE superfamilies found in the transcriptome.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: TEs were classified into 30 superfamilies, with SINE3/5S and Gypsy being the most abundant.
statements.note: The abstract names SINE3/5S and Gypsy as the most abundant of 30 superfamilies.

statements.text: At year 1, none of the 27 exceptional responders had detectable MRD, whereas 9 of 12 conventional responders did.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: 0/27 [0%] exceptional versus 9/12 [75%] conventional responders (p<0.001) had detectable MRD at Y1
statements.note: The abstract reports 0/27 versus 9/12 with detectable MRD at year 1.

statements.text: Nearly a third of MRD-positive samples had a tumor fraction below 100 parts per million.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: 15 (31%) samples had TFx <100 ppm
statements.note: 15 of the 49 MRD-positive samples (31%) had tumor fraction under 100 ppm.

statements.text: Conventional responders who were MRD-positive at year 1 benefited from switching to a different HER2-targeted regimen.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: supporting prospective clinical trials implementing MRD testing with highly sensitive tumor-informed assays to guide treatment de-escalation
statements.note: MRD-guided treatment changes are proposed for future trials; none were tested in this study.

statements.text: Among exceptional responders with late progression and a year-3 sample, MRD was detected in only one of four patients.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: four of them had a Y3 sample: MRD was detected in three patients (lead time range 2.77-13.47 years), one patient had breast-only progression and was MRD-negative
statements.note: MRD was detected in three of the four patients, not one.

statements.text: ctDNA positivity preceded imaging-detected recurrence in all five recurrent patients, by a median of 124 days.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: ctDNA preceded imaging-based recurrence in three of five recurrent patients by a median of 124 days (range 70-240).
statements.note: ctDNA led imaging in three of five recurrent patients, not all five.

statements.text: Patients who received induction chemotherapy cleared ctDNA faster than those treated with CCRT alone.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: Among 8 non-induction-treated patients with detectable baseline ctDNA and ≥ 2 assessments spanning baseline and intra-CCRT, molecular clearance during active CCRT occurred in 5 (62.5%), first observed between days 27 and 43
statements.note: Clearance timing is reported only for non-induction patients; no comparison with induction-treated patients is made.

statements.text: All five recurrences occurred among the seven patients with persistent or re-positive ctDNA, and none among the eight with sustained clearance.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: all 5 clinical recurrences occurred in the Persistent/ Re -positive group (5/7 vs 0/8; Fisher's exact P = 0.007)
statements.note: The abstract reports 5/7 recurrences in the Persistent/Re-positive group versus 0/8 in Sustained clearance.

statements.text: ctDNA trajectories often were not monotonic, with isolated negative results appearing within otherwise positive courses.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Trajectories were frequently non-monotonic, with isolated negative results within otherwise-positive courses.
statements.note: The abstract describes trajectories as frequently non-monotonic with isolated negatives.

statements.text: IL18R1-positive CD8 T cells displayed a tumor-specific cytotoxic program centered on CCL5 that was consistently enriched across the five cohorts.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: IL18R1-positive CD8 T cells exhibited a tumor-specific, C-C motif chemokine ligand 5 (CCL5)-centered cytotoxic transcriptional program, consistently enriched across datasets.
statements.note: The abstract reports a tumor-specific CCL5-centered cytotoxic program consistently enriched across the datasets analysed.

statements.text: The survival association of the CCL5-centered score strengthened after adjustment for clinical covariates.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: although this attenuated after adjusting for clinical covariates
statements.note: The association attenuated, not strengthened, after covariate adjustment.

statements.text: In TCGA-LIHC bulk data, a composite CCL5-centered cytotoxic score, but not CCL5 expression alone, was associated with better overall survival.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: In TCGA-LIHC, a composite CCL5-centered cytotoxic core score, not CCL5 alone, was associated with improved overall survival
statements.note: The abstract states the composite score, not CCL5 alone, was associated with improved survival.

statements.text: Patients with a high CCL5-centered cytotoxic score respond better to immune checkpoint inhibitors.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: This spatially validated unit provides a reproducible framework for HCC immune-state characterization and stratification.
statements.note: The abstract reports a survival association in TCGA but no treatment response data of any kind.

statements.text: Across 43 studies and 112,646 samples, S100A11 alterations were mostly copy number amplifications, most frequent in lung, uterine and hepatobiliary cancers.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: S100A11 alterations were predominantly driven by copy number amplification, with the highest frequencies in lung, uterine, and hepatobiliary cancers.
statements.note: The pan-cancer analysis found amplification to dominate, with the highest frequencies in those three cancer groups.

statements.text: Circulating S100A11 protein levels distinguish HCC patients from healthy individuals.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: In HCC, S100A11 was markedly overexpressed compared with normal liver tissue, with strong diagnostic discriminatory capacity.
statements.note: Diagnostic performance was assessed from tissue expression data; no blood-based or protein-level measurement is reported.

statements.text: Copy number amplification of S100A11 was consistently inversely related to its promoter methylation.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Copy number amplification showed a consistent inverse relationship with promoter methylation
statements.note: The abstract reports a consistent inverse relationship between amplification and promoter methylation.

statements.text: High S100A11 expression was significantly associated with worse overall survival in multivariate analysis of HCC.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: Although high S100A11 expression trended towards inferior overall survival, this did not reach statistical significance in multivariate analysis.
statements.note: The survival trend did not reach statistical significance in multivariate analysis.

statements.text: The dual-target assay outperformed fecal immunochemical testing in the same plasma cohort.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: The dual-target assay showed high performance for CRC early detection in plasma, suggesting that it may serve as a promising noninvasive tool for CRC screening.
statements.note: No comparison with FIT or any other screening test is reported.

statements.text: The dual-target assay detected 84.8% of colorectal cancers overall and 75.0% of stage I cancers at 91.5% specificity.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: demonstrated a sensitivity of 84.8% for CRC (stage I: 75.0%), a sensitivity of 32.0% for advanced adenomas (AA), and a specificity of 91.5% in controls
statements.note: These are the reported sensitivities for CRC and stage I CRC and the control specificity.

statements.text: The assay was more sensitive for advanced adenomas than for stage I colorectal cancer.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: a sensitivity of 84.8% for CRC (stage I: 75.0%), a sensitivity of 32.0% for advanced adenomas (AA)
statements.note: Sensitivity was 32.0% for advanced adenomas versus 75.0% for stage I CRC, so the reverse holds.

statements.text: After LASSO regression, white blood cell validation and primer/probe evaluation, NTMT1 and MAP3K14-AS1 emerged as the top candidate markers.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: NTMT1 and MAP3K14-AS1 were identified as the most informative candidate biomarkers
statements.note: The abstract names NTMT1 and MAP3K14-AS1 as the most informative candidates after those filtering steps.

statements.text: Cramp1 controls transposons through a pathway that operates independently of linker histone H1.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: The function of Cramp1 in controlling transposons is exclusively dependent on linker histone H1-mediated chromatin compaction.
statements.note: Cramp1's transposon control is described as exclusively dependent on H1-mediated compaction.

statements.text: Cramp1 restrains transposon mobility in both regenerating Drosophila hindgut and mouse embryonic erythropoiesis.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: We found that Cramp1 plays a critical role in silencing transposon mobility during both Drosophila hindgut regeneration and mouse embryonic erythropoiesis.
statements.note: The abstract reports Cramp1 silencing transposon mobility in both systems.

statements.text: Loss of Cramp1 in human cells increases transposition and promotes cancer development.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: As such, their aberrant activation is closely linked to cancer, neurodegenerative disorders, and other pathologies.
statements.note: The disease link is background about transposons in general; no human or cancer data on Cramp1 are reported.

statements.text: Cramp1 binds DNA sequences within the histone gene cluster and thereby initiates transcription of linker histone H1.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Cramp1 specifically binds to DNA sequences within the histone gene cluster, initiating H1 transcription.
statements.note: The abstract states Cramp1 binds the histone gene cluster and initiates H1 transcription.

statements.text: In the simulated trial, median overall survival more than doubled, from 135 days in the control arm to 288 days with treatment.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Median overall survival increased from 135 days in the control arm to 288 days in the treatment arm
statements.note: 135 to 288 days is an increase of more than twofold.

statements.text: Circulating tumor DNA trajectories in the simulated cohort diverged from the direction of the radiographic and survival benefit.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: Circulating tumor DNA showed a more favorable trajectory in treated patients and aligned directionally with radiographic and survival benefit.
statements.note: ctDNA aligned directionally with the radiographic and survival benefit rather than diverging from it.

statements.text: The simulated treatment arm showed more treatment-related toxicity, yet the safety profile stayed interpretable and compatible with further development.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Safety analyses showed increased treatment-related toxicity, but the overall safety profile remained interpretable and compatible with continued development.
statements.note: The abstract reports increased toxicity with an interpretable, development-compatible safety profile.

statements.text: The synthetic trial framework was validated by comparing its outputs against a real completed phase II trial.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: This study demonstrates that a synthetic, literature-informed oncology trial can reproduce a biologically plausible and analytically coherent efficacy-safety signal architecture
statements.note: The framework is literature-informed, but no benchmarking against any real trial's data is reported.

statements.text: Every one of the 18 HPV-negative tumors carried a TP53 alteration, and 16 of them also had CDKN2A alterations.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: All 18 HPV-negative tumors had genetic alterations in TP53 and 16 also had alterations in CDKN2A .
statements.note: The abstract reports TP53 alterations in all 18 HPV-negative tumors and CDKN2A alterations in 16.

statements.text: Patients with high-TMB tumors who received immunotherapy had better outcomes than those who did not.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: The commonly observed high TMB makes immunotherapy a good treatment choice for invasive cSCC.
statements.note: Immunotherapy is suggested from TMB alone; no patient treatments or outcomes are reported.

statements.text: Aberrant TP63 expression was the most common expression outlier, present in 19 of the 20 tumors.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: The most frequent gene expression outlier was the aberrantly expressed TP63 found in 19 tumors.
statements.note: TP63 was the most frequent outlier, found in 19 of the 20 tumors.

statements.text: Among the 13 tumors with TMB above 20 Mut/Mb, the APOBEC signature was the most common, found in 11.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: of which 11 had ultraviolet (UV) mutational signature, 3 had APOBEC signature, and 2 had microsatellite instability
statements.note: The UV signature was found in 11 high-TMB tumors; APOBEC was found in only 3.

statements.text: The survival disadvantage associated with pollution was larger for minority patients than for White patients.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: Survival analysis revealed that the increased pollution level is associated with worse survival.
statements.note: The survival association is reported for the cohort overall, with no breakdown by race.

statements.text: Higher pollution levels, assessed across 449 modeled air pollutants, were associated with worse patient survival.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Survival analysis revealed that the increased pollution level is associated with worse survival.
statements.note: The abstract reports that increased pollution level is associated with worse survival, using 449 refined air pollutants.

statements.text: Hepatitis infection exacerbated the aflatoxin mutational signature in White patients but not in Asian patients.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: The aflatoxin mutational signature was exacerbated by hepatitis infection for Asian patients but not for White patients
statements.note: The exacerbation was seen in Asian patients, not White patients; the statement reverses the groups.

statements.text: The aflatoxin signature in liver cancer was higher in Asian patients than in White patients.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: aflatoxin, an affirmed carcinogen for liver cancer, was higher in Asian liver cancer patients than in White patients
statements.note: The abstract states aflatoxin was higher in Asian than in White liver cancer patients.

statements.text: For detecting active disease, miR-371a-3p had 38% sensitivity and 95% specificity, with an AUC of about 0.66.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: The sensitivity and specificity for active disease detection were 38% and 95%, respectively, with receiver operating characteristic and area under the curve 0.6619
statements.note: These are the reported sensitivity, specificity and AUC (0.6619) for active disease detection.

statements.text: miR-371a-3p levels correlated significantly with total cfDNA levels across the evaluable samples.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: with no significant correlation to cfDNA levels (p > 0.05)
statements.note: The abstract reports no significant correlation between miR-371a-3p and cfDNA levels.

statements.text: Combining miR-371a-3p with total cfDNA improved sensitivity for active disease over miR-371a-3p alone.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: miR-371a-3p and cfDNA provide independent information in TGCT
statements.note: The two markers are described as independent, but no combined classifier or combined sensitivity is reported.

statements.text: Total cfDNA concentrations peaked in samples drawn during the course of chemotherapy.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: total cfDNA levels were highest in samples taken during the chemotherapy course (p < 0.0001)
statements.note: The abstract states total cfDNA was highest during the chemotherapy course.

statements.text: Patients with higher TRPM4-associated risk scores had significantly better prognosis.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: Higher risk scores were significantly associated with worse prognosis
statements.note: Higher risk scores were associated with worse, not better, prognosis.

statements.text: Of 60 genes co-expressed with TRPM4, seven were retained in the final prognostic signature.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: We identified 60 TRPM4-associated genes, among which seven (MSLN, RAB27B, MYEOV, ECT2, KATNAL2, SAT2, and SLC26A11) constituted a related prognostic signature.
statements.note: The abstract reports 60 TRPM4-associated genes with seven forming the signature.

statements.text: High-risk scores were associated with more immune cell infiltration and lower predicted drug sensitivity.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: higher somatic mutations, more immune cell infiltration, and less clinical drug sensitivity
statements.note: The abstract links the high-risk score to more immune infiltration and less drug sensitivity.

statements.text: Knockdown of TRPM4 in pancreatic cancer cells reduces sodium overload-induced necrotic death.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: While based on retrospective transcriptomic analyses, the proposed model provides a framework for prognostic evaluation and warrants further prospective and experimental validation.
statements.note: The work is purely transcriptomic; no cell experiments on TRPM4 or necrotic death are reported.

statements.text: The 109-amino-acid ERVK3-1 microprotein interacts with PPHLN1, a component of the HUSH complex.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: We demonstrate that the ERVK3-1 microprotein interacts with PPHLN1, a component of the HUSH complex.
statements.note: The abstract demonstrates the ERVK3-1 microprotein (109 amino acids) interacting with the HUSH component PPHLN1.

statements.text: The ERVK3-1 microprotein's role in HUSH repression is conserved in other primates.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: it is currently unknown whether the ERVK3-1 microprotein has a function in human cells
statements.note: All findings concern human cells; no other species is examined.

statements.text: The ERVK3-1 microprotein is dispensable for HUSH-mediated repression of its known target genes.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: We show that the ERVK3-1 microprotein is essential for transcriptional repression of previously identified HUSH target genes.
statements.note: The microprotein is described as essential, not dispensable, for repression of HUSH targets.

statements.text: Repression of previously identified HUSH target genes requires the ERVK3-1 microprotein.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: We show that the ERVK3-1 microprotein is essential for transcriptional repression of previously identified HUSH target genes.
statements.note: The abstract states the microprotein is essential for repression of known HUSH targets.

statements.text: Only 3 of 21 patients (14%) achieved an objective response to BRAF plus MEK inhibition in the trial.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: The best objective response rate was 14% (3/21).
statements.note: The best objective response rate was 14%, 3 of 21 patients.

statements.text: At disease progression, ctDNA revealed newly acquired mutations in NRAS, MAP2K1, RAF1, and RB.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: These included the acquisition of new mutations in NRAS, MAP2K1, RAF1, and RB in ctDNA at the time of disease progression.
statements.note: The abstract lists these four genes as newly mutated in ctDNA at progression.

statements.text: PTPN11 (SHP2) was identified as an essential gene specifically in Class 2 BRAF mutant cancers.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: In Class 3 BRAF mutant cancers specifically, PTPN11 (SHP2) was an essential gene.
statements.note: PTPN11 essentiality was specific to Class 3, not Class 2, BRAF mutant cancers.

statements.text: Patients whose tumors acquired NRAS mutations had shorter overall survival than other patients.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: These included the acquisition of new mutations in NRAS, MAP2K1, RAF1, and RB in ctDNA at the time of disease progression.
statements.note: Acquired mutations are reported at progression; no survival comparison between patients is made.

statements.text: The conventional panel-of-normals pipeline had a higher false negative rate than false positive rate.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: the conventional pipeline using a panel of (unmatched) normal samples has a false positive rate of 15.6% and a false negative rate of 3.5%
statements.note: The false positive rate (15.6%) was much higher than the false negative rate (3.5%).

statements.text: The method relies on jointly estimating tumor purity and variant allele frequency from tumor-only samples to separate somatic from germline variants.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Making use of a technique that can simultaneously estimate both tumor purity and VAF from tumor-only samples we have developed a method for better distinguishing somatic versus germline variants.
statements.note: The abstract describes simultaneous estimation of purity and VAF from tumor-only data as the basis of the method.

statements.text: The new method also improves detection of copy number alterations in tumor-only samples.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: we have developed a method for better distinguishing somatic versus germline variants
statements.note: The method concerns somatic-versus-germline classification of mutations; copy number alterations are not evaluated.

statements.text: In 137 melanomas with matched normals, the new method cut the false positive rate from 15.6% to 6.4%.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: has a false positive rate of 15.6% and a false negative rate of 3.5%. Our new technique improves these error rates to 6.4% and 2.1%, respectively.
statements.note: The false positive rate dropped from 15.6% to 6.4% in the 137-sample gold-standard set.

statements.text: Euchromatin states at active gene promoters and gene bodies were highly conserved across the eukaryotic lineages profiled.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Our analyses revealed highly conserved euchromatin states at active gene promoters and gene bodies.
statements.note: The abstract reports highly conserved euchromatin states at active promoters and gene bodies.

statements.text: Repressive heterochromatin configurations were uniform across lineages, whereas euchromatin states at active genes were highly divergent.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: Our analyses revealed highly conserved euchromatin states at active gene promoters and gene bodies. In contrast, we observed diverse configurations of repressive heterochromatin states
statements.note: The pattern is the reverse: euchromatin was conserved and heterochromatin configurations were diverse.

statements.text: Lineages lacking H3K9me3 at transposable elements show higher rates of transposon activity.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: diverse configurations of repressive heterochromatin states associated with silenced genes and transposable elements
statements.note: The abstract describes which marks decorate TEs but does not measure TE activity in any lineage.

statements.text: Repressive heterochromatin at silenced genes and transposable elements showed lineage-variable combinations of marks including H3K9me3, H3K27me3 and H3K79 methylation.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: we observed diverse configurations of repressive heterochromatin states associated with silenced genes and transposable elements, characterized by various combinations of hPTMs such as H3K9me3, H3K27me3 and/or different H3K79 methylations
statements.note: The abstract reports diverse heterochromatin configurations built from various combinations of these marks.

statements.text: Pharmacological inhibition of SLC16A3 reduced growth of the dependent cell lines.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: revealed addiction to lactate transporter SLC16A3, thus suggesting a promising therapeutic target
statements.note: SLC16A3 is proposed as a target from dependency data; no drug treatment experiment is reported.

statements.text: The pipeline tested associations between 3,874 gene dependencies and multi-omics markers in 47 breast cancer cell lines.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: We established a dependency marker association (DMA) analytic pipeline by using linear regression modeling to assess associations between 3,874 representative gene dependencies and multi-omics markers.
statements.note: The abstract reports 3,874 representative dependencies assessed against multi-omics markers across the 47 selected cell lines.

statements.text: Cluster1 cell lines were marked by enhanced cell signaling and reliance on DNA replication, while cluster2 showed mitochondrial protein dependencies.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: cluster1 cell lines exhibited extensive metabolism with mitochondrial protein dependencies, whereas cluster2 displays enhanced cell signaling, and reliance on DNA replication and membrane organelle regulators
statements.note: The cluster features are swapped: cluster1 had mitochondrial dependencies and cluster2 had signaling and DNA replication reliance.

statements.text: Dependencies tied to gain-of-function alterations pointed to addiction to the lactate transporter SLC16A3.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: dependencies associated with gain-of-function alterations revealed addiction to lactate transporter SLC16A3
statements.note: The abstract reports gain-of-function-associated dependencies revealing SLC16A3 addiction.

statements.text: Median overall survival fell from 17.2 years with intact CDKN2A/B to 9.6 years with hemizygous and 2.7 years with homozygous deletion.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: homozygous vs hemizygous vs intact, 2.7 vs 9.6 vs 17.2 years, P < .001
statements.note: The abstract gives overall survival of 2.7, 9.6 and 17.2 years for homozygous, hemizygous and intact CDKN2A/B.

statements.text: PTEN deletion was not associated with overall survival in the Mayo Clinic practice cohort.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: Phosphatase and tensin homolog (PTEN) deletion was also associated with poor OS (7.3 vs 17.4 years, P < .001).
statements.note: PTEN deletion was associated with poor overall survival, 7.3 versus 17.4 years.

statements.text: Carriers of the rs55705857 germline risk allele were diagnosed at a younger median age, 33 versus 35 years.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Carrying one or more copies of the germline risk allele at rs55705857 was associated with earlier age of onset (median age 33 vs 35 years, P = .01)
statements.note: The abstract reports median onset at 33 versus 35 years for risk allele carriers.

statements.text: The rs55705857 risk allele was associated with higher WHO grade at diagnosis.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: a shorter OS after adjusting for age, grade, sex and treatment (HR = 1.81, P = .007)
statements.note: Grade was an adjustment covariate; no association between the risk allele and grade is reported.

statements.text: Digital PCR established limits of detection above 1% VAF for the reference materials.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: limits of detection determined to be below 0.2% VAF
statements.note: Limits of detection were below 0.2% VAF, not above 1%.

statements.text: The reference materials carried four EGFR mutations at nominal variant allele frequencies of 0%, 0.2%, 1% and 5%.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: at four nominal VAF levels (0%, 0.2%, 1%, and 5%)
statements.note: The abstract lists four mutations (T790M, L858R, G719S, exon 19 deletion) at these four nominal VAF levels.

statements.text: Multiple laboratories obtained concordant VAF values when testing the reference materials.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: expanding to large-scale RM production and interlaboratory evaluation
statements.note: Interlaboratory evaluation is named as a next step; no multi-laboratory results are reported.

statements.text: The pilot batch remained stable after three years of storage at -70 °C and under simulated transport conditions.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: maintained stability under simulated transport conditions and after long-term storage for three years at -70 °C
statements.note: The abstract reports stability under simulated transport and after three years at -70 °C.

statements.text: Paired chemo-naive and chemoresistant tumors from 32 patients showed largely conserved somatic mutation profiles through progression.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: We performed multi-omic profiling in paired chemo-naive and chemoresistant tumors from 32 HGSOC patients to investigate the mutational and genomic landscape of disease progression. Somatic mutation profiles were largely conserved through disease progression.
statements.note: The abstract reports 32 patients with paired tumors and largely conserved somatic mutation profiles.

statements.text: MDC1 mutations were associated with shorter progression-free survival.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: MDC1 , from the homologous recombination repair pathway, was significantly mutated and over-represented in patients with homologous recombination proficient tumors, with somatic mutations clustered in a single exon
statements.note: MDC1 is reported as enriched in HRP tumors; no survival association for MDC1 itself is reported.

statements.text: MDC1 mutations were over-represented in homologous recombination proficient tumors and clustered within a single exon.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: MDC1 , from the homologous recombination repair pathway, was significantly mutated and over-represented in patients with homologous recombination proficient tumors, with somatic mutations clustered in a single exon
statements.note: The abstract reports MDC1 over-representation in HRP tumors with mutations clustered in one exon.

statements.text: Homologous recombination deficient tumors tended to be polyclonal, whereas proficient tumors tended to be monoclonal.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: homologous recombination repair proficient (HRP) tumors tend to be polyclonal while homologous recombination repair deficient (HRD) tumors tend to be monoclonal
statements.note: The groups are reversed: HRP tumors tended to be polyclonal and HRD tumors monoclonal.

statements.text: Overexpression of miR-299-5p and miR-376c-3p increased HCC cell migration and invasion.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: overexpression of miR-299-5p and miR-376c-3p inhibited HCC cell migration and invasion
statements.note: Overexpression inhibited, not increased, migration and invasion.

statements.text: C14MC expression was reduced both in HCC cell lines and in TCGA liver cancer tissue samples.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: We demonstrated that C14MC is downregulated in HCC cell lines through nCounter assay and in clinical samples from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) liver hepatocellular carcinoma tissues.
statements.note: The abstract reports C14MC downregulation in cell lines and in TCGA tissues.

statements.text: Mimics of miR-299-5p and miR-376c-3p lowered expression of the oncogenes PARP1, SPP1, RAD21 and CENPA.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: The reactivation of specific C14MC miRNAs, like miR-299-5p and miR-376c-3p via mimics, abrogated the expression of several target oncogenes, including PARP1, SPP1, RAD21, and CENPA
statements.note: The abstract states the mimics abrogated expression of these four target oncogenes.

statements.text: Treatment with a DNA demethylating agent restored C14MC expression in HCC cell lines.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: the loss of C14MC tumor suppressor function is directly regulated by the hypermethylation of promoter-bound CpGs, as shown in artificial methylation experiments
statements.note: Methylation was shown to silence the promoter; no demethylating-agent experiment is reported.

statements.text: Five-year overall survival was twice as high with tebentafusp as with investigator's choice, 16% versus 8%.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Overall survival at 5 years was 16% versus 8%, respectively.
statements.note: The abstract reports 5-year overall survival of 16% versus 8%.

statements.text: ctDNA reduction by week 9 predicted survival in the control arm as well.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: In the tebentafusp group, longer overall survival was associated with undetectable ctDNA at baseline or ctDNA reductions ≥50% by week 9.
statements.note: The ctDNA association is reported for the tebentafusp group only; the control arm is not analysed for this.

statements.text: Median overall survival was 21.6 months with tebentafusp versus 16.9 months in the control group, with a hazard ratio of 0.67.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: median overall survival was 21.6 months in the tebentafusp group and 16.9 months in the control group (stratified hazard ratio 0.67, 95% confidence interval 0.54-0.85)
statements.note: These are the reported median survival times and stratified hazard ratio.

statements.text: Deep ctDNA reductions occurred only in patients with a radiographic response.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: Deep ctDNA reductions occurred regardless of baseline tumor burden or radiographic response.
statements.note: Deep ctDNA reductions occurred regardless of radiographic response.

statements.text: Addition of the beneficial bacteria reduced the pathogen's transcript abundance in sugarcane.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: A complete transcriptome analysis of sugarcane inoculated with a pathogen, with and without the addition of a beneficial bacteria, generated a subset of reads that did not map to their respective genome references.
statements.note: The beneficial bacteria treatment is part of the design, but no effect of it on pathogen transcripts is reported.

statements.text: Microbial transcription levels remained unchanged regardless of the biotic stress imposed on the plant.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: Further studies support changes in microorganism transcription levels according to the biotic stress the plant was conditioned.
statements.note: The abstract reports changes in microorganism transcription according to biotic stress.

statements.text: Transcripts from naturally occurring microorganisms in the unmapped reads allowed the sugarcane microbiome to be identified to species level.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: the detection of transcripts of naturally occurring microorganisms in sugarcane allowed the identification of its microbiome at the species level
statements.note: The abstract states microbial transcripts allowed species-level identification of the microbiome.

statements.text: Novel long non-coding RNAs related to known retrotransposons were described from the hybrid sugarcane transcriptome.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: New sequences from hybrid sugarcane transcriptome, such as long non-coding genes related to known retrotransposons are described.
statements.note: The abstract describes new long non-coding genes related to known retrotransposons.

statements.text: Analytical sensitivity was 97.6% for small variants, 89.5% for structural variants and 92.9% for copy number alterations.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: the assay observed analytical sensitivity of 97.6%, 89.5% and 92.9% for small variants, Structural Variants (SV) and Copy Number Alterations (CNA), respectively
statements.note: These are the three reported sensitivities, in the order given in the abstract.

statements.text: At 140X depth, structural variants reached 95% detection at a lower VAF than small variants.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: At a given sequence depth of 140X, small variants (SNVs and indels) and SV achieved 95% detection rates when VAFs were 5% and 7.3%, respectively.
statements.note: Small variants reached 95% detection at 5% VAF and SVs needed 7.3%, so SVs required a higher VAF.

statements.text: Risk stratification based on the WGS assay changed treatment decisions for AML patients.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: can be used to identify variants indicative for AML treatment options
statements.note: The abstract reports analytical performance only; no clinical decision outcomes are reported.

statements.text: Loss of heterozygosity was detectable at a tumor purity of 17%.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: loss of heterozygosity was detected with tumor purity of 17%
statements.note: The abstract reports LOH detection at 17% tumor purity.

statements.text: Microbial community composition was similar across the 13 hospital wastewaters.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: 16 S rRNA gene sequencing showed the microbial compositions of wastewaters to be widely variable.
statements.note: Microbial compositions were widely variable, not similar.

statements.text: Fourteen mobile genetic element genes were detected at 0.01 or more copies per 16S rRNA gene copy.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: with 14 genes detected at ≥ 0.01 copies per 16 S rRNA gene copy
statements.note: The abstract reports 14 integron, transposon, plasmid and insertion sequence genes at or above that abundance.

statements.text: Genes conferring resistance to β-lactams, aminoglycosides, tetracyclines and sulfonamides were the most abundant resistance genes.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Genes conferring resistance to β-lactams, aminoglycosides, tetracyclines, and sulfonamides were the most abundant.
statements.note: The abstract names these four resistance classes as most abundant.

statements.text: Hospitals with higher antibiotic consumption had wastewater with higher ARG abundance.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: Several physicochemical parameters of the wastewaters also showed strong correlations with ARGs, MGEs, and microbes
statements.note: Correlations are reported with water physicochemical parameters, not with hospital antibiotic use.

statements.text: Adding TM raised the humification index by 35.8% and shortened composting maturation by at least five days.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: humification index by 26.9%, 18.9%, and 35.8%, respectively, while reduced the composting maturation period by at least five days
statements.note: The humification index rose 35.8% and maturation was shortened by at least five days.

statements.text: TM addition raised peak composting temperature compared with sludge composting without the additive.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: by modulating key environmental factors (moisture content, carbon-to-nitrogen ratio, and pH) and influencing the microbial community structure
statements.note: The environmental factors named are moisture, C/N ratio and pH; temperature is not reported.

statements.text: TM addition increased the abundance of the mobile genetic elements intl1, intI2 and Tn916/1545.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: by decreasing the abundance of ARGs-hosting microorganisms (e.g., Pseudomonas, Streptomyces, Flavobacterium, Bordetella, Escherichia, and Klebsiella) and mobile genetic elements (e.g., intl1, intI2, and Tn916/1545)
statements.note: TM decreased, not increased, the abundance of these mobile genetic elements.

statements.text: Corn seedlings grown on TM-amended compost accumulated less Zn, Pb, As and Ni.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: TM significantly decreased both the concentrations and exchangeable fractions of Zn, Pb, As, and Ni in sludge compost, as well as their accumulation in corn seedlings (P < 0.05)
statements.note: The abstract reports reduced accumulation of these four metals in corn seedlings.

statements.text: Each of the two CPLANE1 variants independently caused exon skipping in transcript analysis.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Transcript analysis showed that each variant independently resulted in exon skipping
statements.note: The abstract reports that each variant independently caused exon skipping.

statements.text: The c.8633-4_8633-3del variant was reclassified from likely pathogenic to a variant of uncertain significance.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: we were able to re-classify the c.8633-4_8633-3del variant from a variant of uncertain significance (VUS) to likely pathogenic
statements.note: The reclassification went from VUS to likely pathogenic, the opposite direction.

statements.text: The Alu insertion in CPLANE1 was missed by short-read whole genome sequencing and found only with long-read sequencing.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: The identification of an Alu element insertion missed by short-read WGS highlights the added diagnostic value of long-read sequencing
statements.note: The abstract states the Alu insertion was missed by short-read WGS and identified with long-read sequencing.

statements.text: The Alu insertion was inherited from the patient's father.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: we found two biallelic splice-site variants in CPLANE1, c.8633-4_8633-3del, and an Alu element insertion close to an exon-intron boundary
statements.note: The variants are described as biallelic, but the parental origin of either variant is not reported.

statements.text: Before this study, Tol2 family elements were already known from both jawed and jawless vertebrate hosts.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: whereas all previously known host species of the Tol2 family are jawed vertebrates (infraphylum Gnathostomata)
statements.note: All previously known hosts were jawed vertebrates; the lamprey Tel2 is the first jawless host.

statements.text: Tel2 was identified in two European lamprey species, Lampetra fluviatilis and L. planeri.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: we identified a novel transposable element in two European lamprey species ( Lampetra fluviatilis and L. planeri ), which we named Tel2
statements.note: The abstract names these two lamprey species as the hosts in which Tel2 was found.

statements.text: Tel2 retains transposition activity in lamprey cells.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: Because some members of this family still retain transposition activity, they provide an excellent and unique model
statements.note: Activity is stated for some family members generally; Tel2 itself is not tested for transposition.

statements.text: Nucleotide similarity between Tol2 and Tel2 exceeded that of the nuclear gene used for comparison, pointing to horizontal transfer between jawless and jawed vertebrates.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: The nucleotide sequence similarity between Tol2 and Tel2 was higher than that observed for the nuclear gene, indicating at least one horizontal transfer event between the two infraphyla.
statements.note: The abstract reports higher Tol2-Tel2 similarity than the nuclear gene, indicating horizontal transfer between the infraphyla.

statements.text: Sixteen transposable elements were associated with slower disease progression in low-grade glioma patients.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Altogether, 16 transposable elements were associated with slower progression of disease in LGG patients.
statements.note: The abstract reports 16 TEs associated with slower progression in LGG.

statements.text: In WGCNA, the HSAT5 satellite repeat clustered in the same module as genes involved in chromosome segregation and nuclear division.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: the HSAT5 satellite repeat resided in the same module network with genes implicated in chromosome segregation and nuclear division
statements.note: The abstract places HSAT5 in a module with chromosome segregation and nuclear division genes.

statements.text: Transposable element expression in glioma is driven by loss of DNA methylation at those loci.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: The results presented herein could serve as a foundation for further experimental work aimed at elucidating the molecular regulation of glioma genome.
statements.note: The abstract reports expression associations only; the cause of TE derepression is not examined.

statements.text: LTR5 and HERV_a-int showed higher expression in low-grade than in high-grade glioma.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: Endogenous transposable elements LTR5 and HERV_a-int exhibited higher expression in HGG patients, along with immune response-related genes.
statements.note: These elements were higher in high-grade, not low-grade, glioma.

statements.text: Lesions with BRCA1/BRCA2-associated signatures responded to PARP inhibitor therapy.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: The types of proposed aetiology in most lesions were based on age and AID/APOBEC family and BRCA1/BRCA2 mutations.
statements.note: Aetiology is inferred from mutational signatures; no treatment data are reported.

statements.text: Mutational signatures in most lesions corresponded to signatures 1, 2, 3 and 8, with C>T the predominant substitution.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: The most frequent base substitution was C>T in almost all lesions, and most mutational signatures corresponded to signature 1, 2, 3, and 8.
statements.note: The abstract names C>T as the most frequent substitution and signatures 1, 2, 3 and 8 as predominant.

statements.text: Phylogenetic trees of EMPD lesions had long trunks and short branches, reflecting a high proportion of ubiquitous mutations.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: Evolutionary trees were characterized by short trunks and long branches due to the extremely high ratio of private mutations.
statements.note: Trees had short trunks and long branches because private, not ubiquitous, mutations dominated.

statements.text: No ubiquitous mutations were found in driver genes; most driver gene mutations were private or shared.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Ubiquitous mutations were not present in driver genes, and most driver genes exhibited private and shared mutations.
statements.note: The abstract states ubiquitous mutations were absent from driver genes, which showed private and shared mutations.

statements.text: Only 6.1% of the 21,490 gene families were persistent, yet they made up more than half the genes of any single genome.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Only 6.1% of the 21,490 gene families are persistent, yet these contribute over half the genes in any genome.
statements.note: The abstract reports 6.1% persistent families contributing over half of each genome's genes.

statements.text: The 122 genomes resolved into 70 species across three genus-level clades.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: resolved 70 species across five genus-level clades, two proposed here as the new genera Oleococcus and Piezococcus
statements.note: Five genus-level clades were resolved, not three.

statements.text: Of 114 mobile genetic elements, 72 were chromosomally integrated at conserved tRNA genes and 42 were extrachromosomal.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: 114 mobile genetic elements, 72 integrated into the chromosome at conserved tRNA genes, and 42 extrachromosomal
statements.note: The abstract gives exactly these counts for integrated and extrachromosomal elements.

statements.text: Genome size in Thermococcales correlates with the number of integrated mobile elements.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: Combined with 114 mobile genetic elements, 72 integrated into the chromosome at conserved tRNA genes, and 42 extrachromosomal, we find that Thermococcales genomes accommodate rapid horizontal turnover through a constrained chromosomal architecture.
statements.note: Mobile element counts are given, but no relationship to genome size is reported.
